questions.q: If force (F), velocity (V) and time (T) are taken as fundamental units, then the dimensions of mass are:
questions.s: Mass = force ÷ acceleration, and acceleration = V/T. So mass = F ÷ (V/T) = $FV^{-1}T$.

questions.q: If energy (E), velocity (V) and time (T) are chosen as the fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of surface tension will be :
questions.s: Surface tension = energy/area = $E/L^2$, and length L = V × T. So it is $E/(V^2T^2) = EV^{-2}T^{-2}$.

questions.q: If dimension of critical velocity $v_c$ of liquid flowing through a tube is expressed as $(\eta^x\rho^yr^z)$, where $\eta$, $\rho$ and r the coefficient of viscosity of liquid, density of liquid and radius of the tube respectively, then the values of x, y and z are given by :
questions.s: Viscosity is $[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$, density is $[ML^{-3}]$ and radius is $[L]$. Only viscosity has time, so x = 1. Then mass needs y = −1 and length needs z = −1.

questions.q: Planck's constant (h), speed of light in vacuum (c) and Newton's gravitational constant (G) are three fundamental constants. Which of the following combinations of these has the dimension of length?
questions.s: This is the Planck length. Check: hG is $[L^5T^{-3}]$ and $c^3$ is $[L^3T^{-3}]$, so $\sqrt{hG/c^3}$ has dimension $[L]$.

questions.q: A physical quantity of the dimensions of length that can be formed out of c, G and $\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$ is [c is velocity of light, G is universal constant of gravitation and e is charge] :-
questions.s: $e^2/4\pi\epsilon_0$ is force × length², $[ML^3T^{-2}]$. Multiplying by G gives $[L^6T^{-4}]$, its square root is $[L^3T^{-2}]$, and dividing by $c^2 = [L^2T^{-2}]$ leaves $[L]$.

questions.q: A student measured the diameter of a small steel ball using a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm. The main scale reading is 5 mm and zero of circular scale division coincides with 25 divisions above the reference level. If screw gauge has a zero error of − 0.004 cm, the correct diameter of the ball is :-
questions.s: Reading = 0.5 cm + 25 × 0.001 cm = 0.525 cm. The zero error is −0.004 cm, so correct diameter = 0.525 − (−0.004) = 0.529 cm.

questions.q: In an experiment, the percentage of error occurred in the measurement of physical quantities A, B, C and D are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. Then the maximum percentage of error in the measurement X, where $X = \frac{A^2B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3}D^3}$, will be :
questions.s: Multiply each error by its power and add: 2×1 + ½×2 + ⅓×3 + 3×4 = 2 + 1 + 1 + 12 = 16%. Terms in the denominator add too, since errors never cancel.

questions.q: The unit of thermal conductivity is :
questions.s: From $P = KA\Delta T/d$, we get $K = Pd/(A\Delta T)$. Watt × metre ÷ (m² × kelvin) gives $\text{W m}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

questions.q: The main scale of a vernier calliper has n divisions/cm. n divisions of the vernier scale coincide with (n − 1) divisions of main scale. The least count of the vernier calliper is,
questions.s: One main division = 1/n cm, so one vernier division = (n−1)/$n^2$ cm. Least count = 1/n − (n−1)/$n^2$ = 1/$n^2$ cm.

questions.q: Taking into account of the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m − 0.0099 m ?
questions.s: 9.99 − 0.0099 = 9.9801. In a subtraction, keep as many decimal places as the least precise number, 9.99, which has 2. So the answer is 9.98 m.

questions.q: Dimensions of stress are :
questions.s: Stress = force/area = $[MLT^{-2}]/[L^2] = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$.

questions.q: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is :
questions.s: Least count = pitch ÷ number of divisions. So pitch = 0.01 × 50 = 0.5 mm.

Time intervals measured by a clock give the following readings :
1.25 s, 1.24 s, 1.27 s, 1.21 s and 1.28 s.
What is the percentage relative error of the observations ?
questions.s: Mean = 1.25 s. The absolute deviations are 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04 and 0.03, so the mean deviation is 0.02 s. Relative error = 0.02/1.25 = 1.6%.

questions.q: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
questions.s: Mass = F/A, and length goes like $AT^2$. Energy = mass × length² ÷ time² = (F/A)($A^2T^4$)/$T^2$ = $FAT^2$.

questions.q:
A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire
Main scale reading : 0 mm
Circular scale reading : 52 divisions
Given that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire from the above data is :
questions.s: 100 divisions = 1 mm, so one division = 0.01 mm. Then 52 divisions = 0.52 mm = 0.052 cm.

questions.q: If E and G respectively denote energy and gravitational constant, then $\frac{E}{G}$ has the dimensions of :
questions.s: E is $[ML^2T^{-2}]$ and G is $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$. Dividing, the mass powers give $M^2$, length gives $L^{-1}$, and time cancels.

questions.q: The dimensions of mobility of electrons are
questions.s: Mobility = drift speed ÷ electric field. Speed is $LT^{-1}$ and field is $MLT^{-3}A^{-1}$. Dividing gives $M^{-1}T^2A$.

questions.q: Plane angle and solid angle have :
questions.s: Angles are ratios (arc ÷ radius, area ÷ radius²), so they have no dimensions. They still have units: radian and steradian.

questions.q: The dimensions $[MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]$ belong to the :
questions.s: Permeability is measured in newton per ampere squared. That is force per current squared, $[MLT^{-2}A^{-2}]$. Self inductance and flux have extra powers of length.

questions.q: The area of a rectangular field (in $\text{m}^2$) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is :
questions.s: 55.3 × 25 = 1382.5. The answer can only have as many significant figures as the least precise number, 25, which has 2. So it rounds to $14 \times 10^2$ $\text{m}^2$.

questions.q: Match List - I with List - II. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.s: G is $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$ and potential energy is $[ML^2T^{-2}]$. Potential is energy per mass, $[L^2T^{-2}]$, and intensity is force per mass, $[LT^{-2}]$.

questions.q: The dimensions of mutual inductance (M) are:
questions.s: Induced emf = M × (dI/dt), so M = emf × time ÷ current. Emf is $[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$, which gives $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}]$.

questions.q: When the circular scale of a screw gauge completes 2 rotations, it covers 1 mm over the pitch scale. The total number of the circular scale divisions is 50. The least count of the screw gauge in metre is:
questions.s: Pitch = 1 mm ÷ 2 = 0.5 mm. Least count = 0.5 mm ÷ 50 = 0.01 mm = $10^{-5}$ m.

questions.q:
The determination of the value of acceleration due to gravity (g) by simple pendulum method employs the formula,
$g = 4\pi^2\frac{L}{T^2}$
The expression for the relative error in the value of 'g' is:
questions.s: $4\pi^2$ is a pure number, so it adds no error. T is squared, so its relative error counts twice. Errors add, so $\Delta g/g = \Delta L/L + 2\Delta T/T$.

questions.q: The physical quantity that has the same dimensional formula as pressure is :
questions.s: Pressure is force per area, $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$. Young's modulus is stress divided by strain, and strain has no dimension, so it matches pressure.

questions.q:
The percentage error in the measurement of g is:
(Given that $g = \frac{4\pi^2L}{T^2}$, L = (10 ± 0.1) cm, T = (100 ± 1) s)
questions.s: Error in L is 0.1/10 = 1% and in T is 1/100 = 1%. T is squared, so the error in g = 1 + 2 × 1 = 3%.

questions.q: A metal wire has mass (0.4 ± 0.002) g, radius (0.3 ± 0.001) mm and length (5 ± 0.02) cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be :
questions.s: Density = m/(π$r^2$l). Errors: mass 0.002/0.4 = 0.5%, radius 2 × 0.001/0.3 ≈ 0.67%, length 0.02/5 = 0.4%. They add to about 1.6%.

questions.q: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are :
questions.s: Random errors come from unpredictable changes, such as in temperature or voltage supply. They are not the same every time and can be positive or negative.

questions.q: The diameter of a spherical bob, when measured with vernier callipers yielded the following values: 3.33 cm, 3.32 cm, 3.34 cm, 3.33 cm and 3.32 cm. The mean diameter to appropriate significant figures is :
questions.s: Mean = 16.64 ÷ 5 = 3.328 cm. Each reading has 3 significant figures, so the mean is also rounded to 3: 3.33 cm.

questions.q: The mechanical quantity, which has dimensions of reciprocal of mass ($M^{-1}$) is :
questions.s: Gravitational constant is $[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$, so it has $M^{-1}$. Angular momentum, torque and thermal conductivity all have mass to the power +1.
